description: SWEET is a spreadsheet model that estimates emissions of methane, black carbon and other pollutants from every part of a city's municipal solid waste system: collection and transport vehicles, open burning, landfills and dumpsites, composting, anaerobic digestion and waste combustion. It was developed by the US Environmental Protection Agency under the Global Methane Initiative, and is promoted with the Climate and Clean Air Coalition's municipal solid waste work. Users describe their waste generation, composition, collection coverage, fleets and disposal sites, and the tool reports emissions and reductions at project, source and municipality level for a baseline and up to four alternative scenarios, so cities can set targets and track progress. It applies to any city and is distributed free as an Excel workbook, version 5.0, in English, Brazilian Portuguese, French and Serbian. Caveats: default emission factors are generic, results depend on the quality of local waste data, the tool estimates emissions, not service performance, and the Global Methane Initiative website had partial outages when checked. Simulation uses: comparing waste management scenarios for climate adaptation and mitigation plans, appraising investments in landfill gas capture, collection or composting, and building the emissions side of waste system models. Related records: EPA's LandGEM (model-landgem) models landfill gas generation in more detail, and EPA's WARM (model-epa-warm-waste-reduction-model) compares life-cycle emissions of waste management options.
